tabele... Uvozil sem RODBC paket, ker oni xlsreadwrite ni več a voljo
pa ni šlo, potem sem šel v CRAN arhiv in exportiral zip xlsreadwrite
paket pa ga noče importat... Poskušam z ukazom:

> data<-read.table("C:\\Documents and Settings\XP\Desktop\R\tabela,header=T")

javi pa napako in sicer:

Error in file(file, "rt") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: '\D' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
2: '\X' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
3: '\D' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
4: '\R' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
5: unrecognized escapes removed from "C:\Documents and Settings\XP
\Desktop\R\tabela,header=T"
6: In file(file, "rt") :
  cannot open file 'C:Documents and SettingsXPDesktopR
abela,header=T': Invalid argument

Hvala in LP,

Dragan

messages.subject: Re: uvoz podatkov iz excel tabele
messages.body_plain:
Zdravo,

V ukazu si zgrešil narekovaje... narekovaji ti morajo omejit string
(path), ti pa jih imaš še za tistim header=T, ki bi moral biti že
naslednji parameter ukaza read.table.

Zelo enostaven recept je uvoz preko "clipboarda". V Excelu izbereš
podatke, narediš "Copy" (ctrl-c), potem pa v R-u napišeš

moja.tabela = read.table("clipboard",header=T, sep="\t", dec=",")

(tu je predpostavka, da imaš vrstico z imeni stolpcev (header) in da
uporabljaš decimalno vejico in ne piko (dec))

Več podrobnosti lahko dobiš, če napišeš v R-u ?read.table.

Drugače lahko iz excela posnameš worksheet kot "tab delimited text" in
ga isto z read table prebereš v R (namesto "clipboard" lahko uporabiš
funkcijo file.choose(), da potem interaktivno izbereš datoteko).

moja.tabela = read.table(file.choose(),header=T, sep="\t", dec=",")

Tretja rešitev je uvoz podatkov preko R commanderja:

Instalacija: install.packages("Rcmdr")

Vklop: library(Rcmdr)

Potem lahko po menijih najdeš uvoz podatkov.

LP,

Tomaž

messages.subject: Re: uvoz podatkov iz excel tabele
messages.body_plain:
Ahoj,

very interesting question, to which I dread to imagine to know the answer (these sort of things can ruin an evening for a fellow). Red are commands, green are comments and blue is printout.

Basically this is what you do:

> install.packages("RODBC") #this is how you install a package
> library(RODBC) #worth repeating how you load a package
> xls.import <- odbcConnectExcel() #navigate to your .xls file
> xls.import #notice it's just a database connection, not your actual file

To load data from your file, see what sheets are available for selection first (TABLE_NAME).

> sqlTables(xls.import)
                        TABLE_CAT TABLE_SCHEM       TABLE_NAME   TABLE_TYPE
1 C:\\diploma\\rezultati\\analiza        <NA>          checks$ SYSTEM TABLE
2 C:\\diploma\\rezultati\\analiza        <NA>       community$ SYSTEM TABLE
3 C:\\diploma\\rezultati\\analiza        <NA>   environmental$ SYSTEM TABLE
4 C:\\diploma\\rezultati\\analiza        <NA> okoljski_surovo$ SYSTEM TABLE
5 C:\\diploma\\rezultati\\analiza        <NA>         stacked$ SYSTEM TABLE

What you want to do next is import a sheet into your variable something along the lines of:

> communityDB <- sqlFetch(xls.import,  "community") #import.xls is the database connection we created earlier and "community" is the Sheet in the Excel file.

> head(communityDB) #voila! Data ready to be shipped into ordination analyses :)
   F1 Sal_idae Pil_mili Syl_idae Ner_sp# Ner_rava Sab_spin Neo_pseu Ner_zona
1 HM1       12       14        5      13        1        1       28        3
2 HM2      123        5      113      28       44       17        0       15
3 HM3       13       55        8      40        0        2        7       15
4 HM4      141       23       56      91       74        6        0       19
5 HM5        7        0       20      18       11      114        0        7
6 HM6       13       14        0       7        0       39        8        0

Hope that answered your question. This may seem like a lot of hassle (and until you figure it out how to do it it really really is), but can be done really nicely. That aside, I use read.delim. :)

Cheeri-o,
Roman

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dragan,

Both Tomaz and Roman already give some good suggestions how to import data into R. Roman already implicitly told here, but I would like to mention it once more. The warning messages are about the "\". R does not recognize one \, but only two \\. So your import command should be "data<-read.table("C:\\Documents and Settings\\XP\\Desktop\\R\\tabela,header=T")". However, the spaces in the command are also a problem. Before I knew the solutions Tomaz described, I always put my files on one of the c- drive or an external drives. Just to avoid any problems with these spaces.

messages.subject: težave z barchart(lattice)
messages.body_plain:
Pozdravljeni!

Narisati želim T-RFLP profile (kar koli že to je) hkrati za različne
restrikcijske encime z barchart (izvedva xyplot iz paketa lattice).
Imam težave z x-osjo, ki nekako noče prikazovati tistega, kar želim
(itak). Podatki (dolžine fragmentov) so med 0 in 1600, na grafu pa je
iz neznanega razloga privzeta dolžina osi x med 0 in ~250. Na to os so
potem nanizani vsi moji podatki s pravilnimi frekvencami (os y),
vendar so razdalje na osi x med njimi popačene. Enako je problem z
oznakami osi x, ker napisi (labels) ne prikazujejo dejanskih vrednosti
podatkov (0-1600) pač pa tisto arbitrarno skalo (0-250). Ali ima kdo
kakšno idejo, zakaj je temu tako?

(ang.: I wish to draw T-RFLP profiles (lots of them on a single plot)
with barchart (package lattice). X-axis, however, refuses to behave as
expected: my data is between 0 and 1600, however, x-axis appears to be
skewed and plots all my data on an arbitrary scale from 0-250. No
wonder there is also the problem of labels, which show arbitrary
values rather than the values of actual data. Any ideas?)

Tole sem vpisal:

 > CV4<-read.table("clipboard", header=TRUE, dec=",", sep="\t")
 > with(CV4, barchart(freq~fl|encim, horizontal=FALSE, layout=c(1,8),
main="in silico T-RFLP", xlab="dolžina fragmenta", ylab="frekvenca
fragmentov v bazi", scales=list(x=list(relation="same"))))

I know scales (relation="same") is the default value, but I tried it
all the same...

But that aside, let me just say that it's a wonderful thing that so
many people have joined the R-initiative and many thanks to the
initiators!

(S)mejte se,
Luka

messages.subject: Obvestilo o skupini in mailing listi za R samopomoč | R self-help group and mailing list announcement
messages.subject_clean: Obvestilo o skupini in mailing listi za R samopomoč | R self-help group and mailing list announcement
messages.body_plain:
Lep pozdrav,

V četrtek, 5. novembra smo imeli prvo srečanju podporne skupine "Rkoholiki" za vse, ki jih zanima učenje in uporaba programskega paketa R za analizo podatkov. Na srečanju nas je bilo šestnajst, še enajst ljudi pa je javilo, da jih tema zanima, a da se tokrat niso mogli udeležiti. Naslednje srečanje načrtujemo za četrtek, 3. decembra. Da bi zmanjšali število e-mailov, ki jih pošiljamo vsem, smo usposobili mailing listo Rkoholiki, namenjeno vsem diskusijam/vprašanjem/obvestilom v zvezi z uporabo R-a za analizo podatkov in aktivnostmi skupine. Na mailing listo se lahko prijavite tako, da pošljete prazen e-mail na naslov rkoholiki...@googlegroups.com . Na listi nas je že 27 in upamo, da se bo še kdo pridružil.

Lep pozdrav,

Maarten in Tomaž

Hello everyone,

On Thursday, November 5 we had a the first meeting of the Rkoholiki support group for the people interested in learning and using of the R statistical software. Many people showed up (16), and more (11) expressed an interest in the topic. We're scheduling the next meeting for 3rd of December. To limit the number of e-mail messages going to everyone, we created a mailing list Rkoholiki, intended for all discussions/questions/announcements regarding use of R for data analysis and group activities.  You can subscribe by sending an empty e-mail to rkoholiki...@googlegroups.com . We already have 27 members, and we're hoping more will join.

Best regards,

Maarten and Tomaž

messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] težave z barchart(lattice)
messages.body_plain:
Your plot is not working because you're trying to use a barchart for something that a histogram would be needed. If I understand this correctly, barchart function changes the ff into characters, but you want frequencies. If you plot a histogram of CV4$fl you will notice that y axis is about 200, which is about the length of x axis you get with the limited axis in your example.

Here is my code for this lattice plot:

library(plyr) #I need this package to use file.choose() function - you can always use File -> Load Workspace.
load(file.choose()) #I am loading the workspace Luka sent me (.RData)
library(lattice) #we need to load the lattice library to have a faceting plot

#We use with() function to specify which data.frame we are using. The alternative is to use attach() but it can get (really) messy.
We could use histogram() but I find it faster to coarse it into a histogram-like-monster with type="h". If anyone knows how to coarse histogram's bars into lines, I would much appreciate it.
with(CV4, {
xyplot(ff~fl | encim,
horizontal=F, layout=c(2,7), lwd=0.1, type="h")})

We could use histogram() but I find it faster to coarse it into a histogram-like-monster with type="h". If anyone knows how to coarse histogram's bars into lines, I would much appreciate it.

This is the product of the above code <http://rkoholiki.googlegroups.com/web/luka.jpg?hl=en&gsc=Q5B2vAsAAADvPz_NVqCidiqQ7Hoq7Urz>, which is pretty close to what Luka had in mind <https://mail.google.com/mail/?ui=2&ik=22b444de76&view=att&th=125011dd2654f0e8&attid=0.1&disp=inline&zw> with coplot().

To help with the solving process, if you feel attaching your data is neccessary to reproduce your problem, feel free to attach your workspace (File -> Save Workspace and give it an informative name). I would recommend attaching files is by visiting the Anonimni Rkoholiki google groups page <http://groups.google.com/group/rkoholiki/> and uploading your file to the server directly. You can attach the link in your email which will keep the size of your emails down.

Cheereo,
Roman

messages.subject: Obvestilo: 2. sestanek Anonimnih Rkoholikov (3.12.2009)
messages.body_plain:
Dear members,

an entire month has passed since our last meeting. I would like to
extend an official warm welcome to all members of this list and
beyond, to attend the next meeting that will be taking place on
December 3rd, 2009 at the Dept. of biology. The meeting is scheduled
to start at 4pm (16:00 for you metrics) in B6 - the compute room.

Andrej Blejec will be giving a lecture on R basics, which should be of
special interest to novice enthusiasts and workers. "Open mic night"
and discussion will follow. Bring your questions, snippets of code you
may wish to present and a convenient warm beverage holder (Janko Božič
has promised us some home honey).

Hope to see you there.

~~~~

Pozdravljeni,

preminul je že skoraj celi mesec od našega zadnjega snidenja, zato je
čas, da se vnovič srečamo in kako rečemo. Na prvem sestanku je bilo
dogovorjeno, da bo to srečanje ta četrtek, 3.12.2009, ob 16:00 v
računalniški učilnici Oddelka za biologijo.

Andrej Blejec bo predaval o osnovah R-a, pisano na kožo še posebej
tistim, ki jim je R nov. Po predavanju bo mogoče zastaviti morebitna
vprašanja v zvezi z vašim delom. Sledila bo debata, ob kateri si bomo
nalili šalčko čistega. Janko Božič nam je obljubil med, zato ne
pozabite svoje najljubše skodelice.

V upanju, da se vidimo v čim večjem številu
Roman
